notes.okusiga: Also “to climb” or “to get on”: kupanda basi.

guidebook.intro: Most East Africans have a shamba or family in the village. Farming follows the rains, and neighbours help each other.

tips.title: Doing it for someone: -i-, -e-
body: Add **-i-** or **-e-** before the last **-a** and the verb is done for or to someone: **-lima** (farm) → **-limia** (farm for), **-pika** → **-pikia** (cook for), **-leta** → **-letea** (bring to).
With a person inside the verb: **ninakupikia** (I’m cooking for you), **niletee** (bring me), **nitamlimia** (I’ll farm for him or her).

culture.title: Ugali and maize
body: Maize came from the Americas, but **ugali**, a stiff porridge of maize flour, is now the everyday staple of Kenya and Tanzania. A meal without it can feel like no meal at all.

culture.title: Working together
body: At planting and harvest, neighbours often work each other’s fields in turn, with food and drink provided by the host family.
